evaluation.claim: Grace cannot be earned, only received.
evaluation.compressed_claim: Grace cannot be earned, only received.

channel_results.name: External input / dependency honesty
channel_results.reasoning: The claim depends on external theological input (e.g., Christian doctrine) and is honest about that dependency.

channel_results.name: Alignment / reference standard
channel_results.reasoning: Aligns with standard theological reference (e.g., Ephesians 2:8-9). No internal contradiction.

channel_results.name: Truth / signal fidelity
channel_results.reasoning: Claim is a truth claim about the nature of grace; fidelity depends on worldview acceptance.

channel_results.name: Entropy / disorder cost
channel_results.reasoning: Low entropy: simple, clear distinction between earning and receiving.

channel_results.name: Temporal persistence
channel_results.reasoning: Timeless statement; persists across historical and cultural contexts.

channel_results.name: Compression / wisdom density
channel_results.reasoning: High compression: captures a profound theological insight in few words.

channel_results.name: Phase transition / justified regime change
channel_results.reasoning: Implies a phase transition from earning to receiving; justified within its framework.

channel_results.name: Free will / invitation vs coercion
channel_results.reasoning: Invites acceptance, does not coerce; receiving is an act of free will.

channel_results.name: Cross-context binding
channel_results.reasoning: Binds across contexts: theology, ethics, personal experience.

channel_results.name: Integration / whole-system coherence
channel_results.reasoning: Integrates well with broader systems of grace-based thought.
